stories.headline: 5 of 7 people trapped in flooded Laos cave for a week found alive, rescuers say Specialist divers have found five of seven people trapped for a week in a flooded cave in Laos alive, with one rescuer saying their extraction from its...
stories.summary: Specialist cave divers have found five of seven people trapped in a flooded cave in Laos alive. The group of villagers from the central province of Xaysomboun entered the cave over a week ago, but heavy rain triggered flash flooding, blocking their exit. Rescuers, including Laotian and Thai teams, located the five survivors in a deep underground chamber. They were part of a group of nine villagers, but two others are still missing. The rescue operation is ongoing, with efforts focused on extracting the five found alive and searching for the two missing individuals. The cave is located in the central Laotian province of Xaisomboun, where the rescue teams have been working to reach the trapped villagers since the incident occurred.

stories.headline: OpenAI Partners with Tech Giants to Combat AI Election Misinformation OpenAI is teaming up with major social media and technology companies to tackle one of the thorniest problems of the AI era: keeping elections clean when the to
stories.summary: OpenAI is partnering with major tech companies to combat AI election misinformation. The company has joined 26 tech firms in signing a voluntary accord to fight AI-generated misinformation during elections. OpenAI is also backing legislation for AI transparency in politics and partnering with Democracy Works to provide reliable information about voting and registration processes. The company is offering its cybersecurity products to registered voting system manufacturers in the US to support cyber infrastructure defenders and increase transparency around AI-generated content. OpenAI aims to combat misuse by bad actors, monitor bias in its models, and surface reliable information about voting and results. The goal is to keep elections clean and ensure the integrity of the electoral process by promoting transparency and accountability in AI-generated content.

stories.headline: Fact-checking Trump’s claims about Iran war, the economy and the reflecting pool President Donald Trump made false claims about the war with Iran, the economy and other subjects during public comments at a Cabinet meeting on Wednesday.
stories.summary: President Donald Trump made false claims about the war with Iran, the economy, and other subjects during a Cabinet meeting. He repeated assertions concerning the war that were deemed false and mathematically impossible. Trump also discussed his Iran strategy, stating that the upcoming elections would not shape his plan to end the war. Additionally, he claimed that "all of their original leaders" in Iran are dead. Trump's comments were fact-checked and found to be inaccurate. The false claims were made during public comments at the Cabinet meeting, where he also addressed the economy and other topics. The President's statements have been disputed, with fact-checkers highlighting the inaccuracies in his assertions about the war and the economy.

stories.headline: Pope Leo XIV Sparks New Faith Tourism Boom Across Africa Pope Leo XIV’s historic African tour is inspiring countries across the continent to develop Christian pilgrimage tourism, highlighting historic churches, missio
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV's historic 11-day African tour has sparked a new faith tourism boom across the continent. The tour, which covered four nations, was his first visit to Africa as pontiff. During the trip, he made several notable remarks, including criticizing foreigners who exploit Africa's wealth for profit. In response to the tour, African countries are developing Christian pilgrimage routes, heritage churches, and missionary trails to attract international tourists. The initiative aims to promote faith tourism and highlight the continent's rich Christian heritage. Pope Leo XIV's visit has renewed interest in faith tourism, with many nations seeking to capitalize on the growing trend. The development of pilgrimage sites and trails is expected to boost local economies and promote cultural exchange.

stories.headline: Valve's Steam Deck Is Back in Stock, But It Comes With a Shocking Price Hike
stories.summary: Valve's Steam Deck is back in stock after months of unavailability, but with a significant price increase. The 512GB model, previously $549, now costs $789, while the 1TB model has risen from $649 to $949. The price hike is attributed to a memory shortage and rising fuel costs. This increase is substantially higher than the $94 price rise seen earlier this year in Asia, where the distributor Komodo raised prices by ¥15,000. The new prices represent a $240 and $300 increase for the 512GB and 1TB models, respectively. Valve's announcement confirms the Steam Deck's return to availability, albeit at a higher cost to consumers. The price change may impact demand for the handheld gaming device, which had been highly anticipated and popular among gamers.

stories.headline: Two Major Announcements Revealed At Dragon Quest's 40th Anniversary Showcase
stories.summary: Square Enix held a 40th anniversary showcase for the Dragon Quest series, revealing two major announcements. The first announcement is an update on Dragon Quest XII, which has undergone a development restart under a new structure, resulting in a title change from Dragon Quest XII: The Flames of Fate to simply Dragon Quest XII. The second announcement is for a brand-new game, Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World, which is officially coming to Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S. The showcase was part of the series' 40th anniversary celebration, which included a livestream presentation on May 27. The event, titled 'Update from the Dragon Quest Team', provided updates on the series' future developments.

stories.headline: Vadzo Imaging Explains Image Binning Camera Technology for Better Frame Rate and Low-Light Performance
stories.summary: Vadzo Imaging has explained the benefits of image binning camera technology for improved frame rate and low-light performance. The company offers a portfolio of four MIPI camera modules, demonstrating how selecting the right pixel size for real-world lighting conditions enables reliable imaging. Vadzo has launched cameras featuring Sony's Pregius S IMX900 global shutter monochrome sensor and Onsemi's color sensor. The IMX678 STARVIS 2 BSI architecture is highlighted for its low-light performance, surpassing standard front-illuminated sensors by placing the metal wiring layer below the photodiode, reducing light blockage. This design allows more incident light to reach the light-sensitive area, resulting in better low-light performance. Vadzo's camera solutions cater to various applications, including embedded vision, surveillance, industrial, and robotic vision pipelines with stereo vision, structured light, and time of flight architectures.

stories.headline: Asher Pacey Demonstrates Album Surf's Newest Technology: Exo Flex
stories.summary: Asher Pacey is showcasing Album Surf's newest technology, Exo Flex, in a surfboard. The Exo Flex technology stores kinetic energy through load and releases it as drive, enhancing the board's performance. Pacey, from the north coast of New South Wales, Australia, has been working with Album's Matt Parker on surfboard design for years. The collaboration is evident in his surfing, as seen in a video where he effortlessly catches a tube with minimal effort. The Exo Flex technology allows for a more efficient transfer of energy, enabling Pacey to generate speed and drive with less strain. The innovation is a result of Album Surf's focus on blending curves and interaction with water to create high-performance surfboards. Pacey's demonstration highlights the potential of Exo Flex to revolutionize surfboard design and performance.

stories.headline: South Africa name final squad for 2026 FIFA World Cup
stories.summary: South Africa has named its 26-man squad for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The squad includes uncapped defenders Olwethu Makhanya and Bradley Cross, who will make their national team debuts if selected. Makhanya provides an additional centre-back option, while Cross covers left-back, potentially due to Aubrey Modiba's injury. Modiba and Samukele Kabini are also left-back options. Lyle Foster will lead the line, with 19 of the 26 players based in the South African league. Key players include Teboho Mokoena, Themba Zwane, and Zwane, whose experience is seen as vital. The squad has been finalized, with the team set to represent South Africa on the global stage. The final squad selection was announced, locking in the players who will compete in the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

stories.headline: Barcelona in advanced talks over signing Anthony Gordon from Newcastle
stories.summary: Barcelona have agreed a deal worth £69.3m with Newcastle United for England forward Anthony Gordon. The two clubs were in advanced talks over a transfer for the England international, with Barcelona making an offer in the region of £70m. Anthony Gordon is due to undergo a medical in Barcelona on Thursday, and if everything proceeds to plan, he is set to double his wages. The deal is expected to be finalized this week, according to transfer journalist Fabrizio Romano. Barcelona, the La Liga winners, have been pushing hard to seal the deal, and it appears they are close to completing the transfer. The move would see Gordon join the Spanish side, with Newcastle United set to receive a significant transfer fee. The transfer is nearing completion, pending a successful medical.

stories.headline: NZ pair lead fightback against Ireland at Stormont
stories.summary: New Zealand recovered from a poor start to reach 361-5 on the first day of their four-day Test match against Ireland at Stormont. Ireland won the toss and chose to field first in sunny Belfast. A 217-run partnership for the fifth wicket between Ravindra, who scored 142, and Blundell, who remains 142 not out, led the fightback. This is the first meeting between the two sides in Test cricket and also Ireland's first home multiday fixture in two years. Ireland's team has limited experience with red ball cricket, with a rare First Class domestic match taking place in Malahide last week in preparation for the Test match. The strong partnership has given New Zealand a solid foundation on the first day of the match.

stories.headline: Ireland v New Zealand: New Zealand pair lead fightback against Ireland at Stormont
stories.summary: New Zealand recovered from a poor start to reach 361-5 on the first day of the four-day Test match against Ireland at Stormont. After winning the toss, Ireland chose to bowl first, and Mark Adair led the pace attack, taking 3-66. New Zealand were 104-4 at lunch, but Ravindra and Tom Blundell led a fightback, taking the score to 214-4 by tea. Ravindra was eventually caught, but Blundell continued, ending the day on 142*. Ireland missed a chance to dismiss Ravindra earlier when captain Andrew Balbirnie dropped a catch. The Black Caps' strong close was built on a 121 from Ravindra and Blundell's unbeaten 142, setting up an interesting second day, which resumes at 11:00 BST on Thursday.

stories.headline: Suvendu Adhikari Govt’s Tough Stand On Infiltration Triggers 'Return Rush' At Bangladesh Border
stories.summary: The West Bengal government, led by Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, has taken a tough stance on infiltration, triggering a "return rush" at the Bangladesh border. The "Detect, Delete and Deport" policy has led to a significant impact on alleged Bangladeshi infiltrators in North 24 Parganas border areas. Holding centres have been set up for illegal infiltrators, with 12 suspected Bangladeshis detained in Malda and Murshidabad. The government's decision to fence the border has been met with strong protests from Bangladesh, which has urged a humane approach to border disputes. The fencing project aims to curb illegal infiltration and address national security concerns. The situation has led to increased activity at the Hakimpur border check post, with many alleged infiltrators attempting to return to Bangladesh. The West Bengal government remains firm on its stance to tackle infiltration.

stories.headline: Ban cow slaughter in Tamil Nadu with immediate effect, orders Madras High Court
stories.summary: The Madras High Court has ordered a ban on cow slaughter in Tamil Nadu with immediate effect. The court directed that the ban be implemented based on a 1976 government order aimed at increasing milk production. The ban applies to all days, including the eve of Bakrid. Additionally, the court ruled that animal slaughter can only be permitted in designated slaughterhouses. The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court had earlier stayed the Centre's ban on cattle slaughter for four weeks, but this new order specifically targets cow slaughter in Tamil Nadu. The court's directive is intended to protect cows and augment milk production in the state. Authorities are required to enforce the ban and ensure that slaughterhouses operate in accordance with the court's orders.

stories.headline: Government sanctions over 60% manpower boost for Enforcement Directorate
stories.summary: The Union Finance Ministry has sanctioned a cadre restructuring of the Enforcement Directorate, expanding its strength by nearly 60% from 2,029 to 3,256 posts. The Executive cadre will almost double from 1,229 to 2,288 posts. This significant manpower boost is aimed at enhancing the agency's capabilities. Additionally, sanctions were issued on several entities, including the Zindashti Network, which is reportedly connected to Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security. The Zindashti Network was previously sanctioned by the EU last year. These developments indicate a strengthened focus on enforcement and regulatory actions, with the Enforcement Directorate poised to play a more significant role in investigating and prosecuting financial crimes and other offenses. The expansion is expected to enhance the agency's effectiveness in carrying out its mandate.

stories.headline: Hid behind cloak of godman: Rajasthan HC upholds Asaram Bapu's rape conviction but acquits him of gang rape
stories.summary: The Rajasthan High Court has upheld the rape conviction of Asaram Bapu, a self-proclaimed godman, and confirmed his life imprisonment sentence. However, the court acquitted him of gang rape charges and set aside the conviction for criminal conspiracy. Two co-accused in the case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act) were also acquitted. The case pertains to the rape of a minor girl in 2013. The trial court had convicted Asaram in 2018 and sentenced him to life imprisonment. The High Court bench rejected Asaram's plea to set aside his life sentence, confirming that charges of rape, sexual assault under the POCSO Act, and offences under the Juvenile Justice Act were proved. The verdict was delivered after completing hearings on the appeals filed by Asaram and the co-accused.

stories.headline: As geopolitics reshape space, SpinLaunch sees an opening
stories.summary: NASA has partnered with SpinLaunch to test its innovative space launch technology, which utilizes an electric centrifuge to accelerate a launch vehicle to hypersonic speeds. The centrifuge, a giant circular accelerator, aims to launch 200 kilogram satellites into space. In a recent test, SpinLaunch successfully hurled a demo payload, including a NASA test package, high into the sky at high speeds using the oversized centrifuge. This technology differs from traditional rocket launches, instead employing a kinetic launcher to propel the payload. The test, conducted in September 2022, demonstrated the potential of SpinLaunch's whirl 'n' hurl approach, which could revolutionize the space industry with a new and efficient launch method. NASA's involvement marks a significant step forward for the startup's technology.

stories.headline: Nasdaq, S&P Futures Hint At Record Open As AI Mania Turns Wall Street Immune To Geopolitics
stories.summary: Nasdaq and S&P futures are indicating a record open, driven by the ongoing AI mania. Despite unfavorable inflation reports and geopolitical concerns, the US stock market indexes have continued to rise. The S&P 500 recently reached a new high of 7,559, with the Nasdaq also notching fresh records. The Dow has also seen gains, with hopes of war resolution contributing to the upward trend. The AI mania has seemingly made Wall Street immune to geopolitical concerns, with investors focusing on the potential of artificial intelligence to drive growth. As a result, stock market indexes are pushing to new heights, with stock futures hinting at further gains. The trend is being closely watched, with some experts warning of extreme caution due to the rapid pace of the market's ascent.

stories.headline: Details on truce talk progress between the United States and Iran remain
stories.summary: The US and Iran are engaged in truce talks, with the US demanding Iran destroy its three main nuclear sites and deliver enriched uranium. The third round of talks in Geneva ended with the Americans leaving disappointed, while Iran and Oman mediators were more optimistic. Iran has since delivered a 10-point proposal to the US via Pakistan, including a solution to regional conflicts, lifting of sanctions, and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The proposal rejects a temporary ceasefire. Oil prices have fluctuated amid hopes for a deal, with crude plunging after Tehran allowed ships to transit the Strait of Hormuz, only to rebound after the waterway was closed again. A fragile two-week ceasefire remains intact, with the US and Iran potentially returning to negotiations despite failing to reach an agreement in previous talks. The conflict began on February 28.

stories.headline: Declining crude oil prices also offered some support to the wall street indices
stories.summary: Declining crude oil prices have supported Wall Street indices, despite uncertain truce talks between the US and Iran. West Texas Intermediate crude, the US benchmark, fell 6.5% to around $90 a barrel for July delivery. The price drop follows a recent surge that pushed crude benchmarks past $100, raising concerns about global oil supply disruptions in the Middle East. However, the current decline has also led to a slight drop in gasoline prices. Brent crude, the international benchmark, had previously risen above $110 a barrel amid US-Iran war uncertainty, but has since decreased. The fluctuating oil prices have impacted the stock market, with stocks rising as oil prices fall. The ongoing uncertainty between the US and Iran continues to influence oil markets and prices.

stories.headline: Sensex slips 142 points, Nifty ends flat as auto and metal stocks support market The S&P BSE Sensex fell 141.90 points, or 0.19%, to close at 75,867.80. Meanwhile, the NSE Nifty50 slipped just 6.55 points, or 0.03%, to settle at 23,907.15.
stories.summary: The S&P BSE Sensex fell 141.90 points, or 0.19%, to close at 75,867.80, while the NSE Nifty50 slipped 6.55 points, or 0.03%, to settle at 23,907.15. Auto and metal stocks supported the market, but financial services, private bank, and oil & gas shares declined. The Nifty settled below the 23,950 mark. Market experts attributed the range-bound movement to cautious investor sentiment and continued foreign institutional uncertainty. Geopolitical tension in West Asia also contributed to the uncertainty. Despite the decline, media, metal, and auto shares advanced, helping to mitigate the losses. The Indian equity markets ended on a mixed note, with the Sensex declining and the Nifty closing nearly flat. The market's performance was influenced by various factors, including global events and sector-specific trends.

stories.headline: Sensex Ends Lower Amid Banking Drag, Nifty Slips As Iran Tensions Keep Investors Cautious Indian stock markets closed lower in a volatile session on Wednesday as weakness in banking and financial shares weighed on sentiment.
stories.summary: Indian stock markets closed lower on Wednesday due to weakness in banking and financial shares, as well as rising geopolitical tensions between the US and Iran. The BSE Sensex fell 141.90 points to 75,867.80, while the Nifty 50 slipped 6.55 points to 23,907.15. The decline was driven by a drop in banking stocks, which weighed on investor sentiment. Geopolitical tensions between the US and Iran also kept investors cautious, contributing to the market's volatility. The Sensex and Nifty experienced a volatile trading session, ultimately ending lower amid concerns over the US-Iran situation and banking sector weakness. The market's decline reflects the impact of global events on Indian stock markets and the importance of banking stocks in shaping market sentiment.

stories.headline: Market Wrap: Sensex falls 142 points, Nifty holds 23,900; HDFC Bank shares tumble 3% Indian stock market closed in the red, with benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty falling up to 0.2% as Iran-US tensions simmered and rupee declined.
stories.summary: The Indian stock market closed in the red, with the Sensex declining 142 points to 75,868 and the Nifty 50 falling 7 points to 23,907. The decline was attributed to simmering Iran-US tensions and a decline in the rupee. HDFC Bank shares tumbled 3%, contributing to the market's downward trend. The India VIX, a measure of market volatility, was also affected. The market capitalisation declined as a result of the Sensex's 0.2% fall. This comes after a significant decline on May 11, when the Sensex slumped 700 points to close at 77,850 and the Nifty shed 215 points to settle at 23,450. The current market trends and historical performance can be tracked on financial platforms, providing insights into the 30 Sensex stocks and overall market trends. The decline has raised concerns among investors, amid ongoing geopolitical tensions.

stories.headline: Top Gainers & Losers on May 27: JP Power Ventures, Adani Total Gas, HFCL, Swiggy, Suzlon Energy among top gainers On May 27, the Indian stock market showed little movement amidst US-Iran conflict uncertainty.
stories.summary: The Indian stock market showed little movement on May 27, with the Nifty 50 closing down 0.03% and the Sensex falling 0.19% amidst US-Iran conflict uncertainty. Sector performance varied, with Nifty Media rising 3% and Nifty Private Bank among the top decliners. Top gainers included JP Power Ventures, Adani Total Gas, HFCL, Swiggy, and Suzlon Energy. Finolex Industries rose 8.76% to ₹193.74, and Adani Total Gas increased 7.48% to ₹766.45. HAL and HUDCO were also among the top stock movers. In contrast, several stocks posted significant losses, with their share price changes, trading volume, and intraday highs and lows tracked by Yahoo Finance. The mixed market performance reflects the ongoing uncertainty and varied sectoral trends in the Indian stock market. Key stocks and sectors will be closely watched for further developments and potential trading opportunities.

stories.headline: Micron hits trillion dollar value amid AI euphoria
stories.summary: Micron Technology has reached a trillion-dollar market value, driven by the growing demand for AI chips. The company's stock surged 19.3% to $895.88, its highest ever, after an analyst from UBS raised the price target from $535 to $1,625. This increase has propelled Micron into the trillion-dollar club, joining other tech giants like Apple, Meta, and Tesla. South Korea's SK Hynix has also achieved this milestone. The valuation boost is attributed to Wall Street's expectations of continued AI-driven growth in the stock market. Micron's market value is currently near $1.02 trillion, with the company planning to list American depositary receipts this year. The memory-chip maker's stock has seen significant gains, briefly trading at a trillion-dollar valuation and solidifying its position in the elite club of trillion-dollar companies.

stories.headline: American Air (AAL) Sees Robust Demand Even as Consumer Sentiment Falls
stories.summary: American Airlines Group Inc. reports strong demand for travel despite rising jet fuel costs and decreasing consumer confidence in the US. The University of Michigan's Index of Consumer Sentiment dropped to 44.2 in May, its third consecutive monthly decline and the lowest reading since 1952. Rival United Airlines Holdings Inc. also sees robust demand. Surging jet fuel prices are driving up ticket costs, but this has not deterred travelers. The decline in consumer sentiment is attributed to inflation worries, high gasoline costs, and household price pressures. The index fell 10.0% from April and 14.2% from the same period last year, indicating a significant decrease in consumer confidence. Despite this, American Airlines continues to experience strong demand, with the company's bookings and travel plans remaining unaffected by the decline in consumer sentiment.

stories.headline: Canada chooses Sweden's Saab in defence deal over US rivals, PM Mark Carney says
stories.summary: Canada has chosen Sweden's Saab to procure a new fleet of Arctic surveillance aircraft, Prime Minister Mark Carney announced. The decision favors the Stockholm-based company over US competitors. Carney stated that Canada's historically close relationship with the US has been permanently altered, prompting Ottawa to diversify its economic and security relationships. The new Defence Industrial Strategy aims to scale up Canadian industries, simplify equipment procurement for the Canadian Armed Forces, and create jobs. Saab plans to invest in research and development in Canada as part of the deal. Although details on fleet size and contract cost were not disclosed, military officials had previously mentioned plans to buy six early warning aircraft. The move reflects Canada's efforts to expand its partnerships beyond its traditional alliance with the US.

stories.headline: ‘WhatsApp Plus’ subscription launches for $2.99/month, details here
stories.summary: WhatsApp has launched a subscription plan called 'WhatsApp Plus' for $2.99/month in the US. The plan offers exclusive features, including the ability to send premium stickers, change the app's theme, and choose a custom chat wallpaper and icon. The subscription plan is being rolled out globally, following a testing period. WhatsApp Plus is an optional plan, allowing users to continue using the standard version of the app if they choose not to subscribe. The additional features are designed to enhance the user experience, providing more customization options and premium content. The launch of WhatsApp Plus marks a new revenue stream for the messaging platform, which is owned by Meta. The subscription plan is available for users worldwide, with pricing potentially varying by region.
